about.title: Greenfield Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Greenfield's economy runs on hard physical work, from farm fields and packing sheds to small shops along El Camino Real and Elm Avenue. When that work leads to injury, the path forward isn't always obvious. Most of the time, workers' compensation is the only route against your employer, no matter who was careless. But if a piece of faulty equipment, a subcontractor, or someone outside your company played a role, a separate injury claim may also be possible. Monterey County workers deserve clear answers about which path applies to their situation, and how the two systems interact. LawProactive doesn't practice law or charge you anything to get that clarity. We simply connect injured Greenfield workers with an independent attorney who can look at the facts, explain the timelines that matter, and help protect your rights whether the case runs through the workers' comp system, a third-party claim, or both at once.

whyChoose.title: Why Greenfield Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Third-party claims aren't off the table
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent equipment maker, property owner, or outside contractor can still be held separately accountable. An attorney can help sort out whether your situation opens that door.

items.title: Reporting deadlines matter early on
items.desc: California generally requires notifying your employer of a workplace injury within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate your claim. Getting guidance quickly helps protect your options from the start.

items.title: Retaliation is against the law
items.desc: Employers cannot legally punish you for reporting an injury or pursuing a claim. If you're worried about your job while dealing with an injury, an independent attorney can explain your protections.

items.question: I was hurt at a Greenfield job site — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' compensation is your exclusive remedy against your employer, regardless of fault. However, if a third party outside your employer — like equipment maker or a subcontractor — contributed to your injury, a separate claim against that party may be possible. An independent attorney can review the specifics of your Greenfield workplace injury and explain which paths apply.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a third-party claim after a work injury?
items.answer: Third-party injury claims in California generally carry a two-year deadline from the date of the injury. This is separate from workers' comp reporting rules, so it helps to get informed early, especially if machinery, a vehicle, or another company's negligence was involved. Waiting too long can limit your options.

items.question: Are workplace injuries common in Greenfield?
items.answer: Greenfield saw 25 injury collisions and 27 people injured in the most recent reporting year, with reported crashes tending to cluster on Saturday evenings, which can affect workers commuting to and from job sites along corridors like Oak Avenue and El Camino Real. Combined with physically demanding agricultural and industrial work in the area, workplace injuries are a real concern for local workers. LawProactive can connect you with an attorney familiar with claims tied to this kind of local work environment.
